data.name: Hint
data.value: What the company pays you for the rights on works you create, code, a game or content, which you transfer or license to it. Within the limits it stays movable income: the company deducts it in full and withholds 15%, and you are taxed on it apart at 15% plus your municipal surcharge, with no social contributions, on less its flat-rate costs if you hold an attestation du travail des arts. What passes the limits is taxed as your pay.

data.name: Scope
data.value: For works you created yourself, whose rights you transfer or license to your company against a royalty.

data.value: My copyright income of the four previous years averaged at most {0}

data.name: AverageHint
data.value: The royalty stays within its limits only while your copyright income of the four previous years, counted before those limits, averaged at most the year's cap. Netto cannot see it, so it assumes it did until you say otherwise. When it did not, Netto taxes the whole royalty as your pay: the law makes the average a condition without saying more, and that reading never overstates the gain.

data.name: Readings
data.value: Where no text settles a point, Netto takes the reading that never overstates the gain: the 30% is measured on your gross pay on the payslip alone, without benefits in kind or the contributions the company pays for you; neither the royalty nor its part taxed as pay counts in the {0} minimum pay that keeps the reduced corporate rate; the royalty is always taxed apart, never with your other income; the flat-rate costs come off the part within the limits alone, the limits staying on the whole royalty; the royalty is taken as paid on or after 11 June 2026, so the 15% withheld is on its net only with an attestation; and the royalty that follows your pay is measured, like the 30%, on your gross pay on the payslip alone.

data.name: CreativeShareHint
data.value: A royalty that follows your pay reads it, and so do your moves. A ruling of the tax administration accepts a director's royalty of at most 25% of their pay and royalty together, times this share, the basis its rulings take for directors (advance ruling 2026.0484). A royalty that follows your pay is that, kept within the limits. Netto cannot see it, so such a royalty is none until you give it.
